policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 13 Mar close (1x4 3.87, 3x6 4.05, 6x9 4.24, 9x12 4.40 vs WIBOR 3M 3.83) price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC cut by 25bp to 3.75% on 4 Mar (a 'hawkish cut', ING); the projection excludes the war. Glapiński (5 Mar): if things calm within about two months, one more cut is back on the table; no forward guidance. Kotecki (11-12 Mar): the March cut was probably the last this year; Janczyk: wait-and-see for months.
policy.risk_text: Oil and the war set the direction: if Brent stays near $100 the market keeps pricing NBP hikes and the front-end roll-down reverses; a ceasefire would bring cuts back (Glapiński's 'two months'). SAFE politics add a fiscal premium.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar).
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP (MoF figures in Fitch: 7.0% / 6.5% / 6.2% for 2025-27, debt ~70% of GDP by 2027); 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; the President vetoed the SAFE law (12 Mar); the cabinet plans to take the SAFE loan via BGK for the Armed Forces Support Fund (13 Mar).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~38% (25 Feb) financed; MoF cancelled the 11 Mar switch; budget accounts ~PLN 171.6bn at end-February. Moody's reviews Poland on 20 Mar (A2, negative).
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar after holding at 4.00% in January and February; February CPI 2.1% y/y on new weights; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.0%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative (affirmed 27 Feb), Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 13-15 Mar: February CPI 2.1% y/y on the new COICOP 2018 weights (in line; January revised to 2.1%); Domański: MoF will adjust supply to market conditions; Masłowska set a high bar for hikes; the cabinet plans to route the SAFE loan via BGK for the Armed Forces Support Fund. POLGB yields rose 20-50bp in the week and 80-90bp since 2 Mar. Abroad: Brent back above $100; a July ECB hike fully priced; only ~24bp of Fed cuts left for 2026; the US struck Kharg Island.

calendar.plan_text: MoF March plan (27 Feb): sale auctions on 18 and 25 Mar (PLN 7-13bn each; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731 (new 5Y fixed), DS1035, NZ0936 (new 10Y POLSTR floater)) and a switch on 11 Mar buying back OK0426, DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126 and OK0127; no T-bills; WZ sales ended in February. February sales were ~PLN 41bn; ~38% of 2026 needs financed. 9 Mar: MoF cancelled the 11 Mar switch because of market volatility. BGK cancelled its 12 Mar FPC auction (11 Mar). Domański (13 Mar): supply will be adjusted to market conditions.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; in March's sell-off MoF is cutting supply (switch instead of sale, a smaller 25 Mar offer), so remaining dates (18 and 25 Mar) are less of a supply event. Next MPC 8-9 Apr: a hold is expected while the market prices hikes.

facts.core_text: Regime: war shock - oil and global yields up, PLN weaker; the NBP cut to 3.75% and turned wait-and-see while FRAs price roughly 55bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for hikes, the Fed is on hold, the BoE has turned hawkish, the CNB and MNB are on hold. (Erste's CDS/spread table for 13 Mar looked stale or inconsistent, so it is not quoted.) July ECB hike fully priced (13 Mar).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK cancelled the 12 Mar FPC auction and says ~60% of its 2026 FPC financing is already raised (11 Mar).
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
